question: The term ‘protectionist policy’ in the industrial sector in the pre-1990 India refers to __________.

options.text: protecting public sector companies from domestic private sector companies
protecting private companies from incurring losses
protecting domestic companies from the competition of foreign companies
protecting private sector companies from the competition of public sector companies

solution:
The correct answer is __**protecting domestic companies from the competition of foreign companies**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Pdomestic companies from the competition of foreign companies:**

 
• This accurately reflects the core concept of protectionist policies in pre-1990 India.
 
• The government implemented measures like high tariffs, import quotas, and licensing restrictions.
 
• These measures were designed to shield Indian industries from international competition.
 
• The aim was to foster self-reliance and build a strong domestic industrial base.
 
• This included the idea of import substitution, where goods that were being imported, would be made within India.
